note: Re-judged 2026-10-27 by an independent judge (authored none of the change). Section 3: "An implementation SHOULD provide a configuration knob to specify the maximum number of paths to accept from a sender." The tagged units changed only in config spelling: TestParsePeerCapabilityPathsLimit and every case of TestConfiguredPathsLimitOpen now write the knob as limit { receive N; } (receiveLimit(N)) at container and per-family level, which parseAddPathFromTree/addPathReceiveLimit parse to the same values the old scalar gave; every expected family set and limit map is byte-identical and all pass. They remain a strong test of half the sentence: the container knob, the per-family override, and disabled/refused/required families decide the tuples encoded in the OPEN, with an omitted limit advertising none. The other half, "the maximum number of paths to accept", is still not proven by any tagged unit. Phase 3 (9b7673180c) added a receive-side admission (pathsLimitAdmission with a bounded refused set, TestReceiveCeiling* in session_paths_limit_recv_test.go), but its own commit states it is not yet wired into processMessage, so no received path is dropped above the knob on the wire, and none of those tests carries a 3-7 tag. Weak stands until the receive ceiling is reachable from the wire and a tagged test asserts a path above the knob is not accepted.
